assessment_note: Quiz success demonstrates a knowledge answer; playing mastery requires self-assessment or human feedback.

items.question: What is the standard tuning from lowest pitch to highest?
items.explanation: E–A–D–G. Identify the four strings and six instrument parts correctly.

items.question: What should you do before connecting a cable to a loud amplifier?

options.text: Mute it or turn its volume down

items.explanation: Mute it or turn its volume down. Connect and disconnect quietly and find a comfortable clean sound.

items.question: What should mainly support the bass?

options.text: Your strap and balanced body position

items.explanation: Your strap and balanced body position. Play briefly with relaxed shoulders and without gripping the neck for support.

items.question: What should you check before turning a tuning key?

options.text: That it belongs to the string being played
That the amplifier is at maximum
That the string is fretted at twelve

items.explanation: That it belongs to the string being played. Tune all four strings to the correct note and octave with a tuner.

items.question: How should you first increase audible volume?

options.text: Pull every string as far as possible
Adjust the amplifier reasonably while keeping a controlled stroke

items.explanation: Adjust the amplifier reasonably while keeping a controlled stroke. Produce eight clear notes at similar volume without excess tension.

items.question: What is the main aim of this alternating-finger drill?

options.text: Always using the index finger on every note
Consistent timing and volume from both fingers

items.explanation: Consistent timing and volume from both fingers. Play eight bars at 60 BPM with deliberate alternation and even attacks.

items.question: Where should the fretting finger usually sit?

options.text: Just behind the target metal fret
Directly halfway between every pair of frets
Far behind the target fret at maximum pressure

items.explanation: Just behind the target metal fret. Play eight clear fretted notes using comfortable pressure.

items.question: What makes a written rest audible as silence?
items.explanation: Actively damping the strings. Create clear rests with unused strings quiet at 60 BPM.

items.question: At 60 BPM, how long is one quarter-note beat in this exercise?
items.explanation: One second. Play eight bars of quarter notes at 60 BPM with a clear beat-one entry.

items.question: What does 0 on the A-string line mean?

options.text: Use no sound for the entire bar

items.explanation: Play the open A string. Locate every string/fret in the study and explain what zero means.

items.question: Does a louder note necessarily have a higher pitch?

options.text: No; volume and pitch are different

items.explanation: No; volume and pitch are different. Answer at least eight of ten direction trials correctly, then repeat on another day.

items.question: Which is valid evidence of this milestone?

options.text: A controlled performance plus an honest self-check

items.explanation: A controlled performance plus an honest self-check. Demonstrate all open-string milestone criteria in two controlled takes.

items.question: How many quarter-note beats fill a whole note in 4/4?
items.explanation: Four. Hold and stop notes at their correct boundaries for four loops.

items.question: Where does the and of beat one fall?

options.text: Halfway between beats one and two

items.explanation: Halfway between beats one and two. Play four loops of evenly spaced eighth notes at 60 BPM.

items.question: What do the bass-clef lines spell from bottom to top?
items.explanation: G–B–D–F–A. Name four bass-clef notes and locate their corresponding sounding bass positions.

items.question: How is 6/8 commonly felt?

options.text: Two groups of three eighth notes
Three groups of four eighth notes

items.explanation: Two groups of three eighth notes. Explain the grouping difference and play four loops of the 6/8 study.

items.question: Which natural-note pair is one semitone apart?
items.explanation: E and F. Identify eight natural-note locations within frets zero to five.

items.question: What is a good response to an uncomfortable wide reach?

options.text: Use a small controlled hand shift

items.explanation: Use a small controlled hand shift. Make eight accurate, comfortable shifts without losing the pulse.

items.question: What should stay consistent through a string change?
items.explanation: Pulse, volume and muting. Cross all four strings in both directions for four clean loops.

items.question: What does playing staccato mainly change?
items.explanation: Note length and separation. Perform soft/louder and short/long versions without changing tempo.

items.question: What is the root of Em?
items.explanation: E. Play four uninterrupted cycles of G–D–Em–C using correct roots.

items.question: Must the bass copy every kick-drum hit?

options.text: Only if the song has no chords

items.explanation: No; choose a supportive pattern. Maintain a simple root part with a drum loop for one minute.

items.question: What should a useful chart include besides chord names?

options.text: Only the fastest BPM you can play
Section order, bar counts and endings

items.explanation: Section order, bar counts and endings. Follow the 24-bar form and stop at the agreed ending.

items.question: What is the best response to a small slip during this take?

options.text: Add random notes until the band waits
Keep time and recover at the next planned note

items.explanation: Keep time and recover at the next planned note. Play a complete 24-bar arrangement with a clear beginning and ending.

items.question: How many semitones form a perfect fifth?
items.explanation: Seven. Locate one-semitone, major-third, perfect-fifth and octave distances.

items.question: Where are the half steps in a major scale?
items.explanation: Between 3–4 and 7–8. Play C major evenly and identify both half-step positions.

items.question: Which note is the minor third above A?
items.explanation: C. Play A natural minor and explain its relationship to C major.

items.question: Which degree is added to minor pentatonic to make this six-note blues scale?
items.explanation: Flat five. Create two short phrases and distinguish the extra blues-scale note.

items.question: What is the perfect fifth above C?
items.explanation: G. Play root–fifth and root–octave patterns cleanly in two locations.

items.question: Which notes form C minor?
items.explanation: C–Eb–G. Build major and minor triads on two roots and hear the changed third.

items.question: What is vi in C major?
items.explanation: A minor. Translate and play I–V–vi–IV in G and C.

items.question: Which bass note does C/E request?
items.explanation: E. Choose correct bass notes for four slash-chord examples.

items.question: What helps place an offbeat note accurately?
items.explanation: Keeping the subdivision through rests. Repeat the offbeat pattern four times without shifting the pulse.

items.question: In this basic form, which root appears in bars five and six?
items.explanation: IV. Play three complete twelve-bar cycles with correct changes.

items.question: Can two different string/fret positions produce the same pitch?

options.text: Only when both strings are out of tune

items.explanation: Yes. Match at least four of five restricted-range pitches without revealing them first.

items.question: Which note is a strong first choice at a new chord?

options.text: Its root or another intentionally chosen chord tone
Any random chromatic note held indefinitely

items.explanation: Its root or another intentionally chosen chord tone. Perform a 16-bar original arrangement in two keys with dependable roots.

items.question: How many eighth-note triplet slots fit one quarter-note beat?
items.explanation: Three. Switch between straight eighths, triplets and the study swing without changing the quarter-note pulse.

items.question: How many sixteenths fit one quarter note?
items.explanation: Four. Repeat four bars of the sixteenth pattern with clear rests.

items.question: How does a ghost event differ from a rest?

options.text: It makes a muted percussive attack

items.explanation: It makes a muted percussive attack. Distinguish pitched notes, ghost attacks and silence in four clean loops.

items.question: What must be ready for a pull-off to a lower fretted note?

options.text: The lower note finger on the same string
A higher note on another string

items.explanation: The lower note finger on the same string. Demonstrate all three connections slowly with similar note volume.

items.question: Which notes form C7?
items.explanation: C–E–G–Bb. Build and distinguish major7, dominant7 and minor7 on C.

items.question: What bass note is requested by G/B?
items.explanation: B. Play and explain the C–B–A–F bass line under its slash chords.

items.question: What gives an approach note its purpose?

options.text: Its relationship to the target and its resolution
Being played as fast as possible

items.explanation: Its relationship to the target and its resolution. Resolve four approaches to their planned chord roots on time.

items.question: What should you establish before adding chromatic walking notes?

options.text: A different key on each beat
A steady pulse and clear chord changes

items.explanation: A steady pulse and clear chord changes. Play the four-bar walk and explain the two chromatic approaches.

items.question: What can change a repeated-note part without changing its pitches?
items.explanation: Accents and note lengths. Play two contrasting textures with stable timing and quiet unused strings.

items.question: What should happen internally while the bass rests?
items.explanation: The count and listening continue. Maintain a spacious repeated groove for one minute without adding unplanned attacks.

items.question: Which is a useful first step in ear transcription?

options.text: Guess the whole song at full speed
Isolate a short phrase and hear its rhythm

items.explanation: Isolate a short phrase and hear its rhythm. Reconstruct a two-bar original phrase with its main pitches and rests.

items.question: Which is the stronger arrangement choice?

options.text: A new technique in every bar
A controlled variation that supports the form
A fill that loses beat one

items.explanation: A controlled variation that supports the form. Deliver two coherent eight-bar takes with a reliable return after the variation.

items.question: What should be checked before interpreting a number chart?
items.explanation: Its key and notation conventions. Follow a chart with sections, a repeat and a planned ending.

items.question: What is I–V–vi–IV in D major?
items.explanation: D–A–Bm–G. Transpose the progression into two new keys with correct roots.

items.question: What should determine whether to play during a quiet transition?

options.text: The number of notes you know
A rule to play in every bar

items.explanation: The arrangement and leader cue. Play a contrasting verse and chorus and respond to a planned repeat and cutoff.

items.question: After a missed note, what should remain continuous?
items.explanation: Listening and the pulse. Recover from two planned dropouts without shifting the form.

items.question: How many quarter-note beats are in a 5/4 bar?
items.explanation: Five. Play four loops of 5/4 with a clear three-plus-two grouping.

items.question: Which grouping does this study use?
items.explanation: 2+2+3. Maintain the seven-pulse grouping for four loops.

items.question: Which note distinguishes A Dorian from A natural minor?
items.explanation: F# instead of F. Identify the characteristic sixth in Dorian and seventh in Mixolydian.

items.question: What is A7 doing before Dm in this example?

options.text: Acting as a secondary dominant toward Dm

items.explanation: Acting as a secondary dominant toward Dm. Explain the C# in A7 and Ab in Fm in these C-centred examples.

items.question: Can a bass note alone always identify the full chord?

options.text: Only if it is played loudly
No; inversions and shared notes make it ambiguous

items.explanation: No; inversions and shared notes make it ambiguous. Identify four of five restricted-choice progression examples and review misses.

items.question: What should a rhythm transcription include?
items.explanation: Attacks, durations and rests. Reproduce four of five short rhythm patterns after listening.

items.question: What helps a variation remain connected to its motif?
items.explanation: Preserving a recognisable feature. Create two recognisable variations and return on time.

items.question: What is a useful constraint for first improvisation?

options.text: A few chord tones over a known form

items.explanation: A few chord tones over a known form. Improvise three coherent choruses while preserving every chord change.

items.question: Is slap required for every bass arrangement?

options.text: No; it is one optional sound

items.explanation: No; it is one optional sound. Produce eight controlled thumb attacks with clear rests.

items.question: What should be checked when combining slap and pop?
items.explanation: Volume balance and unused-string muting. Play a balanced root-and-octave pattern with clean rests.

items.question: What should be established before speeding up double thumb?

options.text: A relaxed return stroke and even attacks

items.explanation: A relaxed return stroke and even attacks. Play four clean down-up pairs separated by silence.

items.question: What should be prepared before releasing the tapped note?
items.explanation: The intended lower fretted note. Play the three-note tapping phrase with a controlled ending.

items.question: What is the sounding pitch of the twelfth-fret natural harmonic relative to its open string?
items.explanation: One octave higher. Produce and stop a twelfth-fret natural harmonic repeatedly.

items.question: Which symbol normally includes a dominant seventh as well as a ninth?
items.explanation: C9. Explain C9 versus Cadd9 and create a restrained supporting part.

items.question: What is a major tenth?

options.text: A major third plus an octave

items.explanation: A major third plus an octave. Explain how register and spacing change clarity.

items.question: How can you compare two techniques fairly?

options.text: Keep the phrase and listening volume similar

items.explanation: Keep the phrase and listening volume similar. Make an intentional tone choice and explain it with a listening comparison.

items.question: Why record a short test before the full take?

options.text: To check level, noise and monitoring

items.explanation: To check level, noise and monitoring. Save a clean test recording with consistent level and a clear file name.

items.question: Can compression automatically fix wrong notes?
items.explanation: No. Explain one processing choice using an audible before-and-after comparison.

items.question: Which review note is most actionable?

options.text: The entry in bar five is late after the rest

items.explanation: The entry in bar five is late after the rest. Document and improve one specific issue between two takes.

items.question: What is the purpose of learning additional techniques?

options.text: Using every technique in every song

items.explanation: More intentional musical choices. Deliver a coherent arrangement and justify one technique or tone choice.

items.question: What belongs in a useful set plan?

options.text: Keys, tempo units, forms and endings

items.explanation: Keys, tempo units, forms and endings. Prepare a three-piece set plan with complete performance information.

items.question: What should you do if the chart and reference recording differ?
items.explanation: Clarify the intended arrangement. Learn and perform a new short study from its chart and reference.

items.question: Why should split-bar chord durations be marked?

options.text: So players know when the harmony changes
To make the page look busy

items.explanation: So players know when the harmony changes. Produce a chart with no missing chord durations or ambiguous ending.

items.question: What is useful during a soundcheck?

options.text: A representative phrase and clear communication

items.explanation: A representative phrase and clear communication. Complete a brief organised soundcheck with a clear monitoring request.

items.question: What makes a visual cue reliable?

options.text: A complicated gesture no one knows

items.explanation: A shared meaning and attention. Respond to a repeat, dynamic change and cutoff without losing the form.

items.question: What should bass note length respond to?

options.text: A rule that all notes must ring fully

items.explanation: The groove and arrangement. Describe and demonstrate one change that improves the ensemble sound.

items.question: What should you prioritise after an arrangement change?

options.text: Correct form, playable notes and reliable transitions

items.explanation: Correct form, playable notes and reliable transitions. Perform a revised chart with the new key and section lengths.

items.question: Which rehearsal comment is most useful?

options.text: Let us stop together on beat one of bar seventeen

items.explanation: Let us stop together on beat one of bar seventeen. Create a clear preparation list and three actionable rehearsal notes.

items.question: What should be checked after exporting audio?

options.text: The actual exported file and its requested format

items.explanation: The actual exported file and its requested format. Prepare a labelled export that matches a stated mock brief.

items.question: What should a useful performance example show?

options.text: Musical control in a complete context

items.explanation: Musical control in a complete context. Select two complete contrasting examples and explain their purpose.

items.question: What connects an effective practice cycle?

options.text: Observation, focused work, application and review

items.explanation: Observation, focused work, application and review. Write a one-week plan linked to an observed performance need.

items.question: What does this course milestone demonstrate?

options.text: The skills shown in the recorded set and self-review

items.explanation: The skills shown in the recorded set and self-review. Perform and review a complete contrasting set with dependable time, form and endings.
